 Early voting for the 2026 General Election ends tomorrow 
 Early voting for the 2026 General Election ends tomorrow 
 October 30, 2026 
 18 sites available to Wake County voters until 3 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31
 Wake County voters have one more day to cast a ballot during the early voting period for the 2026 General Election. All 18 early voting sites across the county will be open until 7:30 p.m. today and from 8 a.m. until 3 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 31. All eligible voters in line by 3 p.m. Saturday will be allowed to cast a ballot. An interactive map , a live wait time tracker and information about same-day registration are available at WakeVotesEarly.com .
 “Before the early voting period ends, we encourage every voter to check their registration status,” said Wake County Board of Elections Director Olivia McCall. “Eligible voters who still need to register in Wake County have through Saturday to register and vote using same-day registration. And because the last day is typically the busiest, voters can use our live online wait time tracker to find sites with shorter lines.”
 Last Day of Early Voting Checklist
 Before heading out to vote on the last day of early voting, Wake County voters are encouraged to:
 Check your voter registration. Use the NC Voter Search tool to confirm that you are registered at your current Wake County address. Eligible voters who missed the voter registration deadline may still register and vote using same-day registration at any early voting site through Saturday.
 If your registration is not current, come prepared for same-day registration. Same-day registrants must bring acceptable proof of their current residence and complete a voter registration form at the site. Same-day registration is not available on Election Day.
 Bring an acceptable photo ID. All voters will be asked to show an acceptable photo ID when checking in to vote. Most voters will use their NC driver license, but several other forms of photo ID are accepted. Voters who are unable to show an acceptable photo ID may still vote a provisional ballot and complete a Photo ID Exception Form.
 Check wait times before you go. The final day of early voting is typically one of the busiest. Use the live wait time tracker to compare locations and find sites with shorter lines. Wake County voters may vote at any of the 18 early voting locations.
 Be in line by 3 p.m. Early voting ends at 3 p.m. on Saturday. All eligible voters who are in line by 3 p.m. will be allowed to vote.
 Following these steps helps ensure the smoothest voting experience possible, even on the busiest day of voting.

 Absentee Ballot Return Information
 Completed, sealed absentee ballots from Wake County voters may be returned at any early voting site in the county through Saturday by the voter, their near-relative or legal guardian, or someone assisting the voter due to disability. Drop boxes are not permitted by North Carolina law, and anyone delivering an absentee ballot must wait in line to transfer custody of the ballot to an election official.
 Absentee ballots must be received at the Wake County Board of Elections office, located at 1200 N. New Hope Road, Raleigh, NC 27610 , by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3, to be counted, with no exceptions.
 Election Day Reminder
 Registered voters who miss the early voting period may still vote on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3, at their assigned polling place. Polling places will be open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. Unlike during early voting, voters must vote at their assigned polling place on Election Day.
 For more information on upcoming elections and voting, visit ReadyToVote.com .
 About the Wake County Board of Elections
 The Wake County Board of Elections is responsible for conducting all elections held in the county. The Board establishes election precincts and voting sites; appoints and trains precinct officials; prepares and distributes ballots and voting equipment; certifies ballots cast in elections and investigates any voting irregularities.
 The Wake County Board of Elections also maintains voter registration and voting records for more than 860,000 voters. To learn more about the Wake County Board of Elections, follow us on Facebook , Instagram or X , or contact us at voter@wake.gov or 919-404-4040 .
